steps.text: 5:18 P.M. \ Overcast
Primavera City, Iberia, in a certain chapel

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: Oh! How long has someone been at the pews?

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: Ma'am, have you been sitting here this whole time?

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: I passed by just a moment ago, and I didn't see you...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You were focused on this... instrument made of some type of plant tissue, you were using it to polish the floor.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: Er, do you mean my broom? Yes, I'm sweeping the floor right now.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Please excuse me; I did not intend to disturb your work. After all, it seems you'll be busy for quite some time.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: No, it's okay, haha. This doesn't really count as work. I'm just a layman, and I sometimes come help clean the chapel.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: I've never seen you before. Are you an Ægir too?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: ...Ægir?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Your use of 'too' may not be so accurate.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: I—I'm sorry! That's my misunderstanding, then, I didn't mean to regard you as one of us...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Physiologically, you're not mistaken.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: Oh... do you come from another city, then?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You might say so. I only arrived a few months ago.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: Your journey can't have been easy. It never is for us Ægir.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: It has definitely been exhausting.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: If you have any questions, just feel free to ask...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Good. Since you are still willing to call yourself Ægir, I do find something very curious—

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The nation you once belonged to had relentless cleaning devices. Not a speck of dust was allowed to settle on the streets.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: May I ask why you endure such a filthy, inefficient life now?

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: *Sigh*. None of us want to. The disaster fifty years ago changed Iberia.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Iberia?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: No, I was not referring to this dry country.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: Then you mean... all the Ægir settlements from before?

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: I've only ever heard my grandpa mentioning them—*cough*. Ma'am, those underwater cities are all abandoned now. They say they're incredibly dangerous, whether to us islanders, or to Iberia.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You listened to the birds.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Though it only scratches the surface, you still carry a portion of Ægir knowledge and technology.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Why would you consider yourself yet inferior to the barbarians of dry land?

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: It's... not to say we're inferior, but... ma'am, it's best the Penal Battalion doesn't overhear this. It hasn't been easy for us to stay in this city, so near the blockade line...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Cowardice, and misgiving.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: In Ægir, with a child that posed such problems, the parents would be stripped by law of the chance to raise progeny.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: Ah... that sounds a little frightening.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Is it frightening? It seems you've completely forgotten your own originating way of life. The dwellers of land have already assimilated you, whole.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: Living here in Iberia, acting too unlike everyone else is a very risky thing.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I comprehend your choice.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: Ma'am... you seem disappointed, in a way.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Disappointment requires a hope before it.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Perhaps this was not all you brought ashore, but clearly, searching will still require more time.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: Ma'am, I don't think I understand even half of what you're saying.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I am not too familiar with this manner of communication yet.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: Your wording is also... very strange. It reminds me a little of those revues that people liked decades ago...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Are those works of art no longer popular?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: How regrettable. I quite appreciated them.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: So you only intone like this because you like it...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: And you would not achieve rapid grasp of an unfamiliar language by way of audiovisual storage discs?

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: We really couldn't.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Understandable.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: And, generally speaking, it's not because we're too stupid...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Of course there can be other explanations.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: *Sigh*... Ma'am, if I offend you again, I apologize... You seem like you aren't well. Are you ill?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Dry-land pathogens would be hard-pressed to cause any harm to my bodily functions.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: As for emotional ailment, perhaps. After all, it's too dry here.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: I've only ever heard complaints that this season in Iberia is too moist.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: In any case, as long as you aren't sick. Of course, if you feel unwell at all, you can seek help from the priests.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Faith.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You do not harbor faith in science nor technology, nor the nation itself, but invest your ideals in an... impurity that lacks reliability.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Of course, I've recently come to realize, it's also an effective means to accomplish a mutual deception on the power of an informational asymmetry.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: It's possible you've misunderstood. I don't feel that illness can be cured just by thumbing through a holy book or listening to a sermon...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You exceed expectations.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: Ha... haha... Ma'am, you really do have a special sense of humor.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: What I wanted to say was, the people of the Church are very giving, and they've even recently extended shelter to some Ori... er, some sick. They and the sick are all Ægir alike.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Apart from chatting with 'Ægir' such as you, the conduct of the Church you speak of also constitutes my reason for coming here.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: Is that so? You came looking for someone ill?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Supposing who I thought to seek really was here, then...

steps.name: Church Staff
steps.text: Antonio, why does the window on the west have a big hole in it?

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: A hole? It was broken about ten minutes ago, all in a flash. I'd guessed it was the Penal Battalion arresting someone...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: May I suggest to you something?

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: Ma'am, what is it you want to say?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Leave, now.

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: A—An armband? A Battalion armband? Y—You're from the Battalion? It's no wonder you're so peculiar... I never even realized!

steps.name: Pious Youth
steps.text: Officer, th—thank you for letting me free! I'll leave right away!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Remember to close the door.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Not bad. The military organizations of dry land may appear ineffective, the soldiers' technology feeble and pitiful, but to those even weaker, deterrent power is still expressible.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Moreover, I am very glad to see none of you have left.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: This will save me some minor time.

steps.name: Church Staff
steps.text: The scent...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Please come closer.

steps.name: Church Staff
steps.text: *sniff*... *sniff* *sniff*... You're not the Penal Battalion... What do you want?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I had thought you would be capable of more kindly language.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: After all, when I saw how the technology you use was more complete than those runaways', I'd had a shred of hope for you.

steps.name: Church Staff
steps.text: Technology...? We do not understand what you speak of.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Originium. This special energy source, both dangerous and with potential, does not exist on the seafloor.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Curiosity in energy sources is not at all strange.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: No one on dry land has been able to reproduce Ægir's original form, and due to this, I have seen in this nation of Iberia a vast array of technologies composited with no concern for beauty whatsoever.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: However, you are unlike those runaways who forced themselves to integrate into this dry country. You use Ægir technology to purify Originium, and undoubtedly harbor further plans.

steps.name: Church Staff
steps.text: We... help...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Help through giving? Only the naive would believe it.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: They know not where all those sick ultimately disappear to, and I have found traces of Ægir technology on the bodies of those unfortunate experiments.

steps.name: Church Staff
steps.text: You... found them?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: It was in no way difficult.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You aim to transform each and every body. Such technology requires dozens of procedures. And how far have your doings progressed? Perhaps the first procedure, or the second?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The runaways who fled ashore prior to that first contact could not have grasped these procedures.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: As for they, they have occupied the channel between the ocean and the land. If even I have no way to return, none of you could possibly emerge by normal means either.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: How have you, long used to walking on dry land, managed to sustain contact with the ocean?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Or could it be... some have brought the filthiest trash of the sea ashore with them?

steps.name: Church Staff
steps.text: Who are you?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I'm fed up with this game of mutual identification. Such a cliché oughtn't be present in dry land's theater.

Gladiia weightlessly brandishes her lance. An alloy not known to land strikes stone brick at a speed the naked eye cannot perceive. With her at the center, the chapel's entire floor roars as it subsides.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: As I expected.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Did you deliberately construct such an inferior experimentation site below a masquerade of a building, simply to trick the landwalkers' gaze?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Moreover, I'm astonished these petty tricks could actually win such outstanding results.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I once again must reassess the grade of these land nations' organizations.

steps.name: Church Staff
steps.text: *cough*... *cough* *cough*! This weapon of yours! And your strength... is this Originium Arts?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Heh, Originium Arts.

steps.name: Church Staff
steps.text: It—It couldn't be... you... you're...

steps.name: Church Staff
steps.text: If... you're the one the bishops spoke of... then you should've been gravely wounded months ago!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You know of what occurred three months ago on the seafloor?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You've met someone else on the shore.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Who was it—that you met?

steps.name: Church Staff
steps.text: This speed... *wheeze*... *wheeze*... Why were you unmoving before?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I am tired of moving on dry land.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: If standing still will dispose of you shameful ambling trash, why should I waste the further energy?

steps.name: Church Staff
steps.text: I... I do not know... We only guard... You may not destroy this place...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Quite right. You are inferior, and there are limits to the faith you grasp.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Then I can only change to a different topic.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: How many more individuals do you keep on dry land?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: How many more plots do you plot against Ægir?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: And—why—do you research artificial integration of Originium with Ægir bodies?

steps.name: Church Staff
steps.text: *wheeze*... *sniff*... *sniff*... The scent...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Don't waste the energy.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Turning into Sea Terrors will only hasten your deaths.

steps.name: Church Staff
steps.text: It... It couldn't... aaarghhhh—!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Perfect. (Ægirian) I wanted you to die a little faster, anyhow.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: So frail that a single sweep destroys you all.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Urgh—

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: This... gripe in my stomach... is back again. Ever since I came ashore, it hasn't ceased.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: These morons that couldn't even turn fully into Sea Terrors... I see I'm suited only to slaughtering such prey here!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: And these... Ægir who came ashore, they've all become indistinguishable from land-dwellers.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: How long does it take, from leaving the seawater, to the last hint of moisture evaporating from the body?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Whether this end, or another, no matter which...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: No... I cannot...!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: (Vomits)

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: But...

a.text: ...are there others who truly yet live?
If there are, how much time must I spend before I can rescue them?
Gladiia senses her internal temperature still rapidly rising, just as it does on the surface of her body.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Do not stop, you waste.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Though I cannot return to Ægir... no, precisely because I cannot return for now, I must do this.

a.text: Retrieve my hunter. Continue to fulfill my duty.
Fight on without rest or pause.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: ...Who is it?
(Shriek)
I suggest you halt your attack.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Though your strength is uncommon, I'm afraid no one can force me to halt.
Once more, and this chapel will collapse.
You don't pay mind to the Penal Battalion, but I guarantee you, not even you would want to catch the eye of Iberia's Inquisitors.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Land bird...
This meaningless clashing will only slow your search for your comrades.
(Ægirian) Perhaps the nation of the seafloor can still wait.
(Ægirian) For the stranded hunters, there is no such guarantee.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You... You know of Ægir?! You even know our...

Three months oh-seven days ago, fierce oceanbound visions once again manifested in the seas south of Iberia. This information was rapidly curtailed by Iberia's government, but I had my own means to learn of it.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You sought me intentionally. And perhaps you found this place too, like I did?
You can so much as fully understand. I've been waiting for you, and waiting for a very long time.
You've been sent ashore by an exceptional current. It may be extremely painful for you, but for us and Ægir, it is a chance.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You are not hostile. Or else, your revealing this information would have sufficed for me to take your life.
You could do so, but—there is no need for it.
You have amply sensed that I and the sea have no connection. But in reality, between dry land and the ocean, no distance separates.
The ocean in its pride may rarely notice the land, but the land cannot stand by as it sees disaster unfolding in the ocean.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Since my coming here... you are the first to instill awe in me.
You are very well aware, this is not a place for conversation.
Moreover, with how you've dragged your badly injured body to an unfamiliar environment, you cannot hold out for much longer.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Long enough for me to find and cut this trash to pieces.
You know this battle will continue for a very long time.
If they weren't so good at hiding, would Ægir have allowed them to last this long?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: What they are and do does not amount to a threat against Ægir.
You think to draw a distinction between them and they, but I'm afraid that's not how they themselves think.
Will you remain here, continuing to charge me with lance in hand, or shall you leave, together with me, so we can discuss a possible collaboration—
The choice is yours.
Ægir's fate, and that of your comrades, Iberia and even this great land... all rest in your hands.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Before we initiate discussion as to specific matters of cooperation, would you first tell me your name?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Of course.
